title: Core Scientific pivots to AMD with 2.5GW AI data-centre pact months after CoreWeave deal collapsed
excerpt: Nine months after its own shareholders torpedoed a roughly $9bn takeover by CoreWeave, Core Scientific has found a far larger partner in the chipmaker trying to loosen Nvidia’s grip on artificial intelligence. On Tuesday the former bitcoin miner said it had signed a data-centre agreement with AMD that could eventually reach 2.5 gigawatts of capacity across the American […]
content_html:
Nine months after its own shareholders torpedoed a roughly $9bn takeover by CoreWeave, Core Scientific has found a far larger partner in the chipmaker trying to loosen Nvidia’s grip on artificial intelligence.

On Tuesday the former bitcoin miner said it had signed a data-centre agreement with AMD that could eventually reach 2.5 gigawatts of capacity across the American South, and investors treated it as vindication for the deal it had walked away from.

At the core of the arrangement is a set of long-term leases covering 529 megawatts of critical IT capacity, of which AMD has taken 377MW directly while a group of unnamed neocloud operators account for the remaining 152MW.

The sites sit in Pecos and Hunt County in Texas, Muskogee in Oklahoma, Auburn in Alabama, and Dalton in Georgia, and the leases run for 15 years with three five-year renewal options, so the relationship could stretch across three decades. Revenue is expected to start flowing in 2027.

What turns a sizeable colocation deal into a landmark one, at least as both companies framed it, is the option and equity bolted onto it.

AMD has reserved the right to call on up to 1,925MW of further capacity through December 2028, which is how the partnership arrives at its headline 2.5GW, and it receives a warrant for up to 30 million Core Scientific shares at $23.47 apiece, vesting at 12,222 shares for every megawatt it brings online.

About 6.5 million of those shares vested the moment the leases were signed. It is much the same equity-for-capacity structure Nvidia used when it took a $2.1bn warrant in IREN, and it ties a chipmaker’s upside to the fortunes of the landlord housing its silicon.

Neither side put a dollar value on the commitment, and much of the framing came from Core Scientific, which said the new contracts lift its leased footprint to roughly 1.1GW and push its contracted revenue past $24bn.

Those are company figures rather than independently audited ones, so they read as a direction of travel more than a booked result.

The chips, at least, are not in doubt, since the capacity will run AMD’s Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors, and ROCm software.

For AMD the appeal is guaranteed real estate at a moment when it is straining to be taken seriously against Nvidia in both training and inference.

The company has spent the past two years buying and partnering its way toward that credibility, whether by acquiring Silo AI or by promising Anthropic up to two gigawatts of its newest accelerators, and locking in power ahead of demand removes one of the harder bottlenecks.

For Core Scientific, the deal caps a strange and quietly triumphant year. The company spent much of 2025 as CoreWeave’s target, after the GPU cloud offered roughly $9bn in an all-stock deal to fold the miner’s power-hungry sites into its own.

Core Scientific’s investors were unconvinced the price captured the value of that land and power, and on October 30 they voted it down, forcing the company to terminate the merger.

The two are not fully estranged, though, since Core Scientific still hosts CoreWeave’s GPUs under a separate deal worth several hundred megawatts.

The pivot from crypto mining to AI infrastructure is one the whole sector is making, and Nscale’s rapid rise along the same crypto-to-neocloud path shows how richly the market has rewarded it.

One wrinkle is worth watching, because 152MW of the new capacity goes to neocloud operators rather than to AMD directly, and the chipmaker has agreed to provide credit support should one of those tenants default.

AMD, in other words, is partly backstopping the smaller clouds that will run its hardware, a measure of how far it will now go to seed an ecosystem around its chips.

Core Scientific shares jumped as much as 10% on the news, even as AMD slipped more than 5%. The company that could not persuade its owners to sell for $9bn is now, on paper, worth rather more on its own.

content_html_zh:
在其股东挫败 CoreWeave 约 90 亿美元的收购案九个月后，Core Scientific 在这家芯片制造商中找到了一个规模大得多的合作伙伴，试图放松英伟达对人工智能的控制。

周二，这家前比特币矿商表示，它已与 AMD 签署了一项数据中心协议，最终可能在美国南部达到 2.5 吉瓦的容量，投资者将其视为其放弃交易的证据。

该安排的核心是一系列涵盖 529 兆瓦关键 IT 容量的长期租赁，其中 AMD 直接占用了 377 兆瓦，而一组未透露姓名的 neocloud 运营商则占据了剩余的 152 兆瓦。

这些场地位于德克萨斯州的佩科斯县和亨特县、俄克拉荷马州的马斯科吉、阿拉巴马州的奥本和佐治亚州的道尔顿，租约期限为 15 年，并提供三个五年续约选项，因此双方的关系可能会持续三十年。 收入预计将于 2027 年开始流动。

使一笔规模相当大的主机托管交易成为具有里程碑意义的交易的原因是其附带的期权和股权，至少在两家公司的框架中是这样。

AMD 保留在 2028 年 12 月之前进一步增加最多 1,925 兆瓦产能的权利，这就是该合作伙伴关系达到 2.5GW 目标的方式，并且它以每股 23.47 美元的价格获得了最多 3,000 万股 Core Scientific 股票的认股权证，每增加一兆瓦就可授予 12,222 股。

其中约 650 万股股份在租约签署时即归属。 这与英伟达在 IREN 获得 21 亿美元认股权证时所使用的股权换产能结构大致相同，它将芯片制造商的优势与芯片所有者的命运联系在一起。

双方都没有对承诺进行具体定价，大部分框架来自 Core Scientific，该公司表示，新合同将其租赁面积提升至约 1.1GW，并将其合同收入推至超过 240 亿美元。

这些是公司数据，而不是独立审计的数据，因此它们更像是一个行进方向，而不是一个预订结果。

至少这些芯片是毫无疑问的，因为其容量将运行 AMD 的 Instinct GPU、EPYC 处理器和 ROCm 软件。

对于 AMD 来说，在其在训练和推理方面都难以与 Nvidia 抗衡的时刻，其吸引力是有保证的。

该公司在过去两年中一直在通过收购和合作来实现这种信誉，无论是通过收购 Silo AI 还是通过向 Anthropic 承诺提供高达 2 吉瓦的最新加速器，并且在需求之前锁定功率消除了更困难的瓶颈之一。

对于 Core Scientific 来说，这笔交易为奇怪而又悄然胜利的一年画上了圆满的句号。 该公司在 2025 年的大部分时间里都将 CoreWeave 的目标作为了目标，此前 GPU 云以约 90 亿美元的全股票交易将这家矿商的耗电站点并入自己的站点。

Core Scientific 的投资者不相信这一价格能够反映土地和电力的价值，并于 10 月 30 日投票否决，迫使该公司终止合并。

不过，两者并没有完全疏远，因为 Core Scientific 仍然根据价值数百兆瓦的单独协议托管 CoreWeave 的 GPU。

从加密货币挖矿转向人工智能基础设施是整个行业正在做的事情，而 Nscale 沿着同样的从加密货币到新云的路径迅速崛起，这表明市场给予了它丰厚的回报。

有一点值得关注，因为新产能中的 152MW 流向了 Neocloud 运营商，而不是直接流向 AMD，而且这家芯片制造商已同意在其中一个租户违约的情况下提供信贷支持。

换句话说，AMD 正在部分支持将运行其硬件的小型云，这是衡量该公司现在将在多大程度上围绕其芯片打造生态系统的指标。

消息传出后，Core Scientific 股价上涨了 10%，而 AMD 股价却下跌了 5% 以上。 这家无法说服其所有者以 90 亿美元出售的公司现在的纸面价值要高得多。
